series.source_note: Round 11 throughout, except C=2. C=2 is the 2026-08-18 hardening run (c2_atlas_dgx2_20260818.json), not round 8: the certified table originally carried round 8's 38.95 there, which won by 1.004x -- a margin inside either engine's run-to-run spread. Both legs were re-measured back to back on dgx2 on 2026-08-18 (Atlas 15:05, vLLM+MTP 15:20) and that PAIR replaced the earlier pair, which is why the Atlas number rose to 41.02 while the paired vLLM number fell to 37.11 and the margin moved to 1.105x with non-overlapping distributions. A round-11 C=2 exists at 40.42 (l38_r11_c2.json) but has no same-day vLLM leg, so it is not publishable as a pair. See RESULTS.md, C=2 HARDENED.

series.label: vLLM + MTP
series.cli: vllm serve --model unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --served-model-name unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-prefix-caching --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
series.instrument_note: prompt_mode essay, ADDED 2026-09-21 so the live gate record can be drawn against this bar: ladder-baselines.js treats an undeclared REQUIRED axis as a DIFFERENCE, never a match, so without it an Atlas run measured on exactly this instrument could never be paired with it. HOW MUCH OF THIS IS FACT: the harness reads PROMPT_MODE = os.environ.get('W55_PROMPT_MODE', 'essay') and appends SUFFIX_ESSAY unless it is 'count'. Two of the four driver revisions behind this manifest are recoverable from this repo's own history and both read exactly that -- 1f10d4887b is bench/ladder38/harness_w55_conc_ladder.py at 60370b953 (the 2026-08-18 C=2 pair, BOTH legs) and 41e242c072 is the copy committed today at 452493a35 -- and SUFFIX_ESSAY is byte-identical between them. For those rungs this is a FACT, read from the source that ran. The other two revisions (6412b12d4d, the vLLM reference legs; 1c77e1d8e9, Atlas rounds 7-11) were never committed at this path, so for their rungs it is DERIVED: the recorded env does not set W55_PROMPT_MODE, and the raw files carry isl/osl/reps/warmup/temperature/seed and chat_template_kwargs but no prompt_mode. The completion distributions corroborate it -- the count fixture stops far short of the budget, while these runs sit at the 1024 budget with deterministic minima of 691 (C=128) and 753 (C=64). Re-check if a raw file is ever replaced; a harness that RECORDED the mode would make the whole manifest a fact.
series.source_note: The apples-to-apples reference: ctx 2048, batch cap 128, util 0.85, fp8 KV, prefix caching, thinking off and MTP K=4 -- every axis matched to Atlas. vLLM at its best, not a handicapped baseline.

series.label: vLLM + MTP (energy)
series.cli: vllm serve --model unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --served-model-name unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-prefix-caching --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
series.instrument_note: Measured 2026-09-21 on spark-43fa to give the Cost tab a vLLM leg that carries JOULES; the existing vllm-mtp legs are throughput-only. Same engine (vLLM 0.27.1), same checkpoint, same instrument as vllm-mtp -- the CLI above is that leg's, verbatim. Throughput landed at 94-98% of it on every rung (18.99/36.26/68.21/117.20/189.70 vs 19.72/37.11/71.61/124.48/197.03), a different day and box, which is the agreement that makes the energy quotable rather than the point of the run. prompt_mode essay: the pinned harness defaults to it (harness_w56_conc_ladder.py, PROMPT_MODE = os.environ.get("W55_PROMPT_MODE", "essay")) and the run's env did not set it. Driver 664302439b is harness_w56, the energy harness; w55 is the one without power_window. parity is `matched` because the instrument IS matched -- every axis equals vllm-mtp's. It is not the published ratio's reference all the same: ladder-build.mjs picks that from the FULL-LADDER baselines only, and this leg is C=1..16. `unmatched` would have been the wrong label twice over: it means 'differs on these named axes' and requires parity_deltas, which this leg has none of.

series.label: vLLM + MTP
series.parity_note: Matched to the Atlas MoE ladder recipe adjudicated by the bench-parity oracle on 2026-09-19 before the run: ctx 2048, batch cap 128, util 0.85, bf16 KV, MTP K=4, thinking off, presence/frequency penalties 0.0, and Atlas pinned to fifo scheduling (its MoE recipe defaults to slai, which vLLM has no counterpart for). That is the configuration an Atlas leg at this instrument must serve to be scored against this series; no such leg exists yet.
series.build_note: Read from `docker image inspect vllm/vllm-openai:latest` on dgx2 on 2026-09-19, not remembered: image id sha256:2c211a1273b48e8929f893b267aeb1509e6b84654cdbde1bad56d79e3964224d, label ai.vllm.image.tag=vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1, vLLM commit 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac, created 2026-08-11. It is the same digest the dense ladder's vLLM legs ran, and a container from it logs `version 0.27.1` at startup.

kernel_override.what: vLLM is NOT running its own default FP8 MoE kernel on this hardware. Its default FP8 block-scale MoE path selects DeepGEMM; these two variables force the Marlin FP8 path instead.
kernel_override.why: DeepGEMM crashes at WEIGHT LOAD on GB10 (SM121), before any inference: the first attempt of the evening died at 79% of the load. The same SM120/SM121 incompatibility already recorded for the TRTLLM, CuteDSL, DeepGEMM and Triton MoE backends; only CUTLASS and Marlin work on this box.
kernel_override.error: deepgemm_post_process_weight_scale_block -> transform_sf_into_required_layout: RuntimeError: Assertion error (deepgemm-src/csrc/apis/layout.hpp:60): Unknown SF transformation
kernel_override.scope: A kernel selection, not a workload axis: it moves nothing the parity oracle adjudicates, but a reader comparing engines deserves to know.

series.cli: docker run --network host --gpus all --ipc=host -v /home/claude/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 -e VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1 vllm/vllm-openai:latest --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enable-prefix-caching --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype auto --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
series.speculation: vLLM's own MTP drafter, K=4 (--speculative-config method=mtp, num_speculative_tokens=3)
series.instrument_note: kv_cache_dtype is bf16 although the command says `--kv-cache-dtype auto`: auto takes the model dtype, and `--dtype bfloat16` is set, so the KV cache is bf16 BECAUSE the dtype is bfloat16. Spelled `bf16` because that is how an Atlas gate record writes serve_overrides.kv_cache_dtype, which is what this fingerprint is compared against; vLLM's own spelling is bfloat16. No prompt_mode: the ladder harness has no fixture, it sends a nonce-prefixed padded prompt, so a gate record (natural fixture) can never fingerprint as this instrument. prompt_mode is essay because the pinned harness defaults to it (bench/ladder38/harness_w55_conc_ladder.py:75, PROMPT_MODE = os.environ.get("W55_PROMPT_MODE", "essay")) and this series' recorded env (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1) does not set it. DERIVED, NOT RECORDED: the raw file carries isl, osl, reps, warmup, temperature, seed and chat_template_kwargs but not prompt_mode, so re-check this if the raw file is ever replaced -- a harness that recorded it would make this a fact instead of an inference. It is declared because ladder-baselines.js treats an undeclared axis as a DIFFERENCE, never a match: without it a future concurrency-sweep-moe gate record measured on this exact instrument could never be drawn against this bar.

unmeasured.reason: The ladder stops at C=16 because of memory, not because of time. GB10 carries 121.7 GB of UNIFIED memory shared between CPU and GPU -- there is no separate VRAM to fall back on. At C >= 32 the vLLM + MTP working set (per-sequence KV cache plus MTP's speculative draft state) outgrows what that shared pool can carry alongside the host, and because the pool is shared, exhausting it takes the whole machine down rather than failing a single allocation: three physical powercycles in one day, at the safe util 0.85 and with --max-num-seqs already capped. We did not isolate it further because every attempt costs the box. These rungs were deliberately not run. They have no value here: not zero, not interpolated, and the generator refuses a raw file that contains them.

series.source_note: One-shot: measured once, on 2026-09-19 on dgx2, and never re-run. Every rung comes from the single raw file vllm_moe_c1_16.json (sha256 7788d19a16bb32466a53f72fc13c70c8f9352fb888b758f786a54c1a6b7ad648, byte-identical to dgx2:/home/claude/ladder-moe-baseline/). Two earlier attempts the same evening produced no numbers and are not here: one died in DeepGEMM at weight load (kernel_override), one ran the ladder against a serve whose harness preflight had failed (no first token; TypeError on ttft_p50_ms). Zero request errors at every rung.

qwen36-35b-a3b.subject_note: No series has role "subject": no Atlas run exists at this instrument for this checkpoint. This manifest deliberately mirrors bench/ladder38/published.json so that when one does, it is added as a series with role "subject" whose sources name its raw harness files, and gen-ladder.mjs scores the pair with the same code it scores the dense ladder with. Until then the generator emits no rows and no summary for this ladder, and the site says so instead of drawing a zero.
